Tenant.//: Fallback company/agency/user used ONLY when Authentication:AllowHeaderFallback is on, which requires the Development environment. A valid token always wins; without one and without the fallback, an unauthenticated request cannot resolve a tenant and is rejected.

Logging.//Console: IncludeScopes is required, not cosmetic. The correlation middleware puts the correlation id in a log SCOPE, and the simple console formatter does NOT render scopes by default — so without this every log line looks identical and the correlation id never reaches the output, which is precisely what ties a caller's report to a server log entry.
Logging.//HttpLogging: The bare Microsoft.AspNetCore rule is Warning, which SUPPRESSES the request log this API configures — leaving it enabled but silent. The category is raised explicitly above. Each line is method, path, status and duration only; headers and bodies are excluded on purpose, because the token endpoint takes a password in its body. NOTE: this comment key sits at the Logging level, NOT inside LogLevel. Every key inside LogLevel is read as a category name whose value must be a log level, so a comment there is a startup failure rather than a comment.
Logging.//EventLog: Disabled on purpose. The default Windows EventLog provider writes to the Application log, which requires elevated access; when it is denied the logging call throws and takes the request down with it. Nothing here depends on the event log.

Hosting.//: HTTPS redirection is OFF by default. Behind a TLS-terminating proxy, redirecting produces a loop or breaks a health probe, so it is a deployment decision. When enabled, an HTTPS port MUST be determinable (here or via an https:// url); otherwise the host refuses to start, because the middleware would silently redirect nothing.

Cors.//: Origins allowed to call this API from a browser. EMPTY BY DEFAULT, which means no cross-origin access at all — a browser front end on any other port is blocked until its origin is listed here. Credentials are not enabled, so bearer tokens are what authorise a call.
